scope: CH4 only, first physical capture xryrmxjl, channel 0; not a suite pass
conclusion: Length-expired DAC-on restart phase follows continuing-counter prediction; inactive-freeze rejected at 12 discriminating gaps. DAC-off controls disagree with continuing reference and with the freeze-at-length-expiry candidate. Hidden LFSR continuation is not identified.
method: First isolated negative noise step after retrigger, midpoint of extrapolated local pre/post baselines; no case alignment or template phase fitting. One 32-anchor hardware affine map from initial NR42 DAC-on CPU-scheduled edges; same map for all 48 cases. One constant reference-renderer delay from the corresponding reference-only edges.

uncertainty.bound_status: Engineering sensitivity allowances, NOT statistical confidence intervals or demonstrated hard bounds. Include one native sample, baseline/ringing sensitivity, calibration drift and analog transfer; unknown hardware latency remains a caveat.

caveats: NR42 DAC-on and a noise step need not have exactly identical analog group delay. Packet-only calibration is an independent sensitivity check, not a guarantee of CPU-cycle accuracy.
APU log timestamps are GB_run instruction boundaries, not bus-cycle timestamps. Onset numbers are delay relative to an effective equal-write calibration, not cycle-exact internal transitions.
A single 48 kHz capture cannot establish a hardware revision population or hidden LFSR/feedback-latch evolution. Trigger resets downstream state; reference and hidden-run audio are byte-identical.
DAC-off nearly gap-independent output is compatible with stopped/reset/rephased counter behavior; it does not uniquely distinguish those mechanisms.
Active-muted gap 0 is about 74-75 T later than its gap 1536 repeat; retain this small control anomaly rather than declaring exact agreement.
Final NR52-off edges were not used: nearby noise edges and emulator highpass clearing distort several endpoints.
Packet integrity and recording quality are outside this delegated analysis; existing packet identities are used as timing anchors only.
